Friday Events
Friday only - Conformation Handling Seminar
Learn the Tricks of the Trade!! Presented by Charlene Schlueter & Cheryl Hart. Depending on the weather the seminar will be held in either the conformation ring OR in the main pavilion. 4:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. Free Seminar - no sign up required.
Fun on Friday (Non-Sanctioned)
Hay Stack Hunt Challenge (Barn)
Come for a Roll in the Hay. Let your dog's shake off their travel cobwebs & get used to the rats in cages hidden on the course. Same description as the Sat & Sun Hay Stack Hunt except the Friday event will only have 1 rat on the course. Friday Only, event runs from 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. All dogs/all breeds 6 months & older are welcome to compete. Cost is $5.00 per dog. Enter in Trial Vault in the "Add On" section OR enter/pay that day (cash/check only) at the Hay Stack Hunt Challenge entry table. Top 3 eligible fastest times will win prizes. Event is limited to a maximum of 60 dogs. See our Trial Flyer for more information.
Brush Hunt Challenge
Friday Only, event runs from 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. All dogs/all breeds 6 months & older are welcome to compete. Cost is $5.00 per run. Enter in Trial Vault in the "Add On" section OR enter/pay that day (cash/check only) at the Brush Hunt Challenge entry table. Top 3 eligible fastest times will win prizes. Event is limited to a maximum of 60 runs. See our Trial Flyer for more information.
Midwest Mayhem Challenge
Friday only, event runs from 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. This is our version of Thunder Tunnel. All dogs/all breeds, up to 15" height, 6 months and older are welcome to compete. Cost is $5.00 for 2 back-to-back runs. Entry can be made in Trial Vault "Add On" section OR enter that day at the MW Mayhem table (cash or check only). Top 3 eligible fastest times will win prizes. See our Trial Flyer for more info.

Youth
No entry fee. The sanctioned Youth Division is open to JRTCA child and/or youth members in the following age brackets: Child Handler (ages 5 thru 9) and Youth Handler (ages 10 thru 16). A child/youth exhibitor’s age is determined as of January 1st of the current calendar year except for those children turning five years of age. They may begin competing in Child Handler any time following their firth birthday. All exhibitors in the Youth Division must be current JRTCA members, either under a Family membership or under an individual Youth membership. Youths or their families applying for a JRTCA membership at a Sanctioned Trial will be allowed to enter classes at that trial. Youth exhibitors must compete in a minimum of Youth Handling and Youth Go-to-Ground to qualify for the Youth High Score & Reserve. Child exhibitors must compete in a minimum of Child Handling and Child Go-to-Ground to qualify for the Child High Score & Reserve (non-sanctioned). A tie will be broken with the final decision made by a conformation judge other than the judge of the day. The tiebreaker takes place in the conformation ring and is determined at the judge's discretion by the exhibitor's handling/presentation of his/her terrier, by the answers to the judge's questions, or by a combination of the two. Note: If there is no other available conformation judge on the grounds, then the judge of the day will determine the tiebreaker. For a full set of rules or to see the JRTCA Child & Youth Handler Handbook & Study Guide go to: https:// www.therealjackrussell.com , under Trial - click on Youth

Racing
JUDGE'S BRIEFING AT 8:15 A.M. Adult terriers may not cross-enter between regular racing classes, veteran racing classes and senior racing classes. Terriers must be muzzled for racing. Plastic muzzles or close-ended cloth muzzles only. Black, brown, clear or white muzzles are acceptable; no colored basket or softie muzzles allowed. No figure 8 or open-ended or Baskerville open-ended muzzles will be allowed. Racing champions are determined by a run-off of the first-place terrier in each class in each section. Qualifications for Championship Run Off: A. Terriers must place 1st in a Flat or Hurdle race FInal to qualify for Championship Run Offs. B. A terrier MUST ENTER AND FINISH in both, at least one flat AND one hurdle race at the beginning level based on trial entries (heat, semi, final). C. A terrier must continue to advance, if qualified, to all additional semi-final heats up to the final champion race. If injured, the terrier is then finished and cannot race in final. D. A FINISHED race is when the terrier runs down the track unassisted (by owner or anyone else) with a secured muzzle to the backside of the barrier. E. In the event a terrier does not meet all the above criteria, the second-place terrier in the final of that class (either flats or hurdles) will qualify for the championship run off if they meet the criteria as outlined above. Racing Ribbons Presentation time will be announced during racing. The rulebook is available at www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/rulebook.php. For other information about racing, go to www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/racing.php.

Go-to-Ground
A timed event that simulates the terrier's natural instinct to hunt. The terrier enters an artificial den/tunnel to demonstrate its working ability. Schooling prior to the competition is not permitted (any violation of this rule shall result in disqualification from G-T-G at this trial). Terrier may switch from one type of work to another (examples: baying to concentrated stare to digging to baying. Work is defined as baying, digging, concentrated stare, whining or biting at the bars. A break in work is defined as ceasing work for a period of more than 10 seconds. Leaving the quarry is defined as moving back in the tunnel away from quarry and out of view of the judge. The judge may halt the work if the judge believes the terrier is injuring itself. For Championship Certificate classes, a copy of the certificate must be submitted with pre-entry (preferred - enter in Trial Vault) or be shown to the Den Steward at the time of the class. No cross entering between Certificate classes.

Super Earth
A more challenging G-T-G course is used for this Super Earth course with a series of false entrances and/or false tunnels and dens. Open to any terrier, 6 months and older. Schooling prior to the competition is not permitted (Any violation of this rule shall result in disqualification from Super Earth at this trial). Terrier may switch from one type of work to another (examples: baying to concentrated stare or digging to baying.) For Championship Certificate classes, a copy of the certificate must be submitted with pre-entry (preferred - enter in Trial Vault) or be shown to the Den Steward at the time of the class. No cross entering between Certificate classes. Timing for all Super Earth classes: One second per foot of tunnel to reach quarry; may leave and re-enter the earth multiple times until quarry is reached; work quarry for one minute without a break in work and without leaving quarry. Terrier is not to leave quarry once it is reached.

Trail & Locate Obstacle Course (Non-Sanctioned)
This Trail & Locate Obstacle course is a non-sanctioned event which simulates a real environment where a dog must follow a scent while navigating through a course of obstacles & challenges to locate and open on live quarry. The course will be scented using rat urine. Dogs have a total of 2 minutes to find the quarry. When directed by the Judge, owners will release their dog at the starting gate. The dog must then follow the scented course. The scent course travels over, through, under, and around a wide variety of obstacles such as tunnels, hay bales, brush piles, fencing, equipment, machinery & other items. The dog's time starts when they are released at the starting gate. The timer stops when the Judge determines that the dog has found the quarry. If a dog bypasses or skips an obstacle, one second is added to their time (for each obstacle that is bypassed/skipped). As determined by the Judge, dogs who reach the quarry and actively work it by barking will have three seconds subtracted from their time. No cross entering between classes.

Agility
All terriers must be at least one year of age to compete in JRTCA Agility or practice on any equipment. Dogs may run naked or wear one flat collar without tags. No other accoutrements are allowed. No food or toys are allowed within 10 feet of the ring. Exceptions are that toys are allowed for the class “A Way to Play”. A Beginner Agility certificate may be earned prior to competing in Advanced Agility & for Agility High Score Champion & Reserve. Move ups from Beginner Agility to Advanced Agility are allowed from trial to trial. (Example: 2nd Beginner leg is earned at Saturday’s trial; the team could move to Advanced Agility for Sunday’s trial). As a JRTCA certificate has not been issued both qualifying score sheets must be presented to move up. Advanced Agility competitors may cross enter the Beginner Agility class for Exhibit Ony (FEO) to be used as a warmup run. No ribbons will be rewarded, and no paperwork completed for an FEO run. Teams with two scores of 190 or greater in the agility classes (Beginner and Advanced) are eligible for agility certificates. Teams with one qualifying score of 200 in Jumpers are eligible for the Jumpers certificate. Adult dog jump heights will be: Under dogs will jump 8" and Over dogs will jump 12". At the Owner's decision Veteran dogs jump height will be 8" or 12". All Senior dogs regardless of height will jump 4". Veteran & Senior dogs are allowed 10% more time. For a complete set of rules, go to www.therealjackrussell.com under Trial - click on Agility.

Nose Work
Saturday Only - Open to dogs six months and older who are capable of alerting to the target odors. Level 1 target odor is birch. There is one hide in each Level 1 search, with maximum time limit of two minutes. Level 2 target odors can be birch, anise and clove. There are two hides in each level 2 search, with search times between 2:30 and 4:00 minutes. A Level 1 title is not required to enter Level 2 classes. Owners may enter two dogs in the same class but must either have someone else handle the second dog or wait until the end of the class to allow the judge time to relocate the hide. Teams must go through the start-line markers and call "alert" when hides are found. Search areas will be clearly marked. In Level 1 searches, one incorrect call is allowed but incurs a 5-second fault. For Level 2 searches, handlers must call "finish" after the second hide is found. An incorrect call in Level 2 ends the search and results in a non-qualifying run. Time faults incurred for dropped food, failure to go through start-line marker, excessive disturbance of search area, incorrect call in Level 1 and failure to call "finish" in Level 2 searches. Eliminating (pee, poop or vomit) in a search area ends the search and results in a non-qualifying score and no placement. Consult the rulebook for more detailed information: https://www.therealjackrussell.com/download/nosework2025.pdf First through sixth place ribbons for each class determined by correct calls with fastest time first. Champion and Reserve Champion ribbons awarded to top two JRTs in Level 1 and top two JRTs in Level 2 by combining scores for all elements/classes. Teams with no faults considered first.

Not your mother's regular old barn hunt!! 2 rats on the course each day - in wire cages (protected by wooden boxes) - more open and evident to the dogs & much more fun to find. Designed & put together full of bales, tunnels, platforms, ramps & other structures. New course each day. No cross entering between classes. See the Trial Flyer for more details. Rules and time limits will be posted near the course.

Brush Hunt (Non-Sanctioned)
Brush hunt is an above-ground hunting simulation held in a fenced area. One camouflaged tube containing a live quarry is hidden within the brush area. The challenge is for the dog to use natural instincts to successfully locate and work the quarry. Dog must find the quarry in the shortest amount of time. The clock starts when the judge is ready and signals you to release your dog at the gate. All four paws must be on the ground before you release your dog. The judge stops the clock when your dog has found the tube. You do not enter the course, but you can encourage your dog verbally. No hand signals allowed. The dog must locate the tube to have a qualifying time. No cross-entering between classes. Maximum time allowed is two minutes.

Youth
No entry fee. The sanctioned Youth Division is open to JRTCA child and/or youth members in the following age brackets: Child Handler (ages 5 thru 9) and Youth Handler (ages 10 thru 16). A child/youth exhibitor’s age is determined as of January 1st of the current calendar year except for those children turning five years of age. They may begin competing in Child Handler any time following their firth birthday. All exhibitors in the Youth Division must be current JRTCA members, either under a Family membership or under an individual Youth membership. Youths or their families applying for a JRTCA membership at a Sanctioned Trial will be allowed to enter classes at that trial. Youth exhibitors must compete in a minimum of Youth Handling and Youth Go-to-Ground to qualify for the Youth High Score & Reserve. Child exhibitors must compete in a minimum of Child Handling and Child Go-to-Ground to qualify for the Child High Score & Reserve (non-sanctioned). A tie will be broken with the final decision made by a conformation judge other than the judge of the day. The tiebreaker takes place in the conformation ring and is determined at the judge's discretion by the exhibitor's handling/presentation of his/her terrier, by the answers to the judge's questions, or by a combination of the two. Note: If there is no other available conformation judge on the grounds, then the judge of the day will determine the tiebreaker. For a full set of rules or to see the JRTCA Child & Youth Handler Handbook & Study Guide go to: https:// www.therealjackrussell.com , under Trial - click on Youth

Racing
JUDGE'S BRIEFING AT 8:15 A.M. Adult terriers may not cross-enter between regular racing classes, veteran racing classes and senior racing classes. Terriers must be muzzled for racing. Plastic muzzles or close-ended cloth muzzles only. Black, brown, clear or white muzzles are acceptable; no colored basket or softie muzzles allowed. No figure 8 or open-ended or Baskerville open-ended muzzles will be allowed. Racing champions are determined by a run-off of the first-place terrier in each class in each section. Qualifications for Championship Run Off: A. Terriers must place 1st in a Flat or Hurdle race FInal to qualify for Championship Run Offs. B. A terrier MUST ENTER AND FINISH in both, at least one flat AND one hurdle race at the beginning level based on trial entries (heat, semi, final). C. A terrier must continue to advance, if qualified, to all additional semi-final heats up to the final champion race. If injured, the terrier is then finished and cannot race in final. D. A FINISHED race is when the terrier runs down the track unassisted (by owner or anyone else) with a secured muzzle to the backside of the barrier. E. In the event a terrier does not meet all the above criteria, the second-place terrier in the final of that class (either flats or hurdles) will qualify for the championship run off if they meet the criteria as outlined above. Racing Ribbons Presentation time will be announced during racing. The rulebook is available at www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/rulebook.php. For other information about racing, go to www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/racing.php.

Go-to-Ground
A timed event that simulates the terrier's natural instinct to hunt. The terrier enters an artificial den/tunnel to demonstrate its working ability. Schooling prior to the competition is not permitted (any violation of this rule shall result in disqualification from G-T-G at this trial). Terrier may switch from one type of work to another (examples: baying to concentrated stare to digging to baying. Work is defined as baying, digging, concentrated stare, whining or biting at the bars. A break in work is defined as ceasing work for a period of more than 10 seconds. Leaving the quarry is defined as moving back in the tunnel away from quarry and out of view of the judge. The judge may halt the work if the judge believes the terrier is injuring itself. For Championship Certificate classes, a copy of the certificate must be submitted with pre-entry (preferred - enter in Trial Vault) or be shown to the Den Steward at the time of the class. No cross entering between Certificate classes.

Super Earth
A more challenging G-T-G course is used for this Super Earth course with a series of false entrances and/or false tunnels and dens. Open to any terrier, 6 months and older. Schooling prior to the competition is not permitted (Any violation of this rule shall result in disqualification from Super Earth at this trial). Terrier may switch from one type of work to another (examples: baying to concentrated stare or digging to baying.) For Championship Certificate classes, a copy of the certificate must be submitted with pre-entry (preferred - enter in Trial Vault) or be shown to the Den Steward at the time of the class. No cross entering between Certificate classes. Timing for all Super Earth classes: One second per foot of tunnel to reach quarry; may leave and re-enter the earth multiple times until quarry is reached; work quarry for one minute without a break in work and without leaving quarry. Terrier is not to leave quarry once it is reached.

Trail & Locate Obstacle Course (Non-Sanctioned)
This Trail & Locate Obstacle course is a non-sanctioned event which simulates a real environment where a dog must follow a scent while navigating through a course of obstacles & challenges to locate and open on live quarry. The course will be scented using rat urine. Dogs have a total of 2 minutes to find the quarry. When directed by the Judge, owners will release their dog at the starting gate. The dog must then follow the scented course. The scent course travels over, through, under, and around a wide variety of obstacles such as tunnels, hay bales, brush piles, fencing, equipment, machinery & other items. The dog's time starts when they are released at the starting gate. The timer stops when the Judge determines that the dog has found the quarry. If a dog bypasses or skips an obstacle, one second is added to their time (for each obstacle that is bypassed/skipped). As determined by the Judge, dogs who reach the quarry and actively work it by barking will have three seconds subtracted from their time. No cross entering between classes.

Agility
All terriers must be at least one year of age to compete in JRTCA Agility or practice on any equipment. Dogs may run naked or wear one flat collar without tags. No other accoutrements are allowed. No food or toys are allowed within 10 feet of the ring. Exceptions are that toys are allowed for the class “A Way to Play”. A Beginner Agility certificate may be earned prior to competing in Advanced Agility & for Agility High Score Champion & Reserve. Move ups from Beginner Agility to Advanced Agility are allowed from trial to trial. (Example: 2nd Beginner leg is earned at Saturday’s trial; the team could move to Advanced Agility for Sunday’s trial). As a JRTCA certificate has not been issued both qualifying score sheets must be presented to move up. Advanced Agility competitors may cross enter the Beginner Agility class for Exhibit Ony (FEO) to be used as a warmup run. No ribbons will be rewarded, and no paperwork completed for an FEO run. Teams with two scores of 190 or greater in the agility classes (Beginner and Advanced) are eligible for agility certificates. Teams with one qualifying score of 200 in Jumpers are eligible for the Jumpers certificate. Adult dog jump heights will be: Under dogs will jump 8" and Over dogs will jump 12". At the Owner's decision Veteran dogs jump height will be 8" or 12". All Senior dogs regardless of height will jump 4". Veteran & Senior dogs are allowed 10% more time. For a complete set of rules, go to www.therealjackrussell.com under Trial - click on Agility.

Brush Hunt (Non-Sanctioned)
Brush hunt is an above-ground hunting simulation held in a fenced area. One camouflaged tube containing a live quarry is hidden within the brush area. The challenge is for the dog to use natural instincts to successfully locate and work the quarry. Dog must find the quarry in the shortest amount of time. The clock starts when the judge is ready and signals you to release your dog at the gate. All four paws must be on the ground before you release your dog. The judge stops the clock when your dog has found the tube. You do not enter the course, but you can encourage your dog verbally. No hand signals allowed. The dog must locate the tube to have a qualifying time. No cross-entering between classes. Maximum time allowed is two minutes.

MW Mayhem (Non-Sanctioned)
Midwest Mayhem is our version of Thunder Tunnel a fun and interactive tunnel with one side open for viewing your terrier. Each entry includes two back-to-back runs. Tunnels will have obstacles & course changes that your terrier will need to problem solve through. No cross entering between classes.
